newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Parry sees 4 to 5 percent growth in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Parry sees 4 to 5 percent growth in Mexico.

text.p: San Francisco Federal Reserve Bank President Robert Parry Monday said he was quite encouraged about conditions in Mexico and that it was possible that growth would be in the four to five percent range in 1997 and 1998.
"If we look at the situation today, we are quite encouraged about prospects in Mexico," he told a Chamber of Commerce group here.
He said that between the second quarter of 1995 and the second quarter this year, Mexico grew at a rate of about seven percent.
"If you look at some of the forecasts, and I've seen a few, it looks as though Mexico could grow about four to five percent in '97 and '98," he said.
He told the group that if this occurs, the impact would be favorable to the United States, particular in the border states,
"Good economic success in Mexico is going to be very helpful to trade between our two countries," he said.
